column3: The Hebrew says he ordered the book brought and that its contents were being read before him; BSB includes reading in the order itself.
The Hebrew says the men sought to stretch out a hand against the king; BSB describes conspiracy to assassinate him.
The Hebrew calls the attendants the king’s young men, his servants; BSB uses attendants.
The Hebrew says let him come; BSB commands others to bring him in.
The Hebrew says Haman spoke in his heart; BSB renders this as thinking to himself.
The Hebrew names a royal crown on its head; BSB calls it a royal crest.
The Hebrew says not to let a word fall from all he spoke; BSB renders this as not neglecting anything suggested.
The Hebrew separately describes mourning and a covered head; BSB combines them as a head covered in grief.
The Hebrew begins the advisers’ statement with if Mordecai is of the seed of the Jews; BSB states since Mordecai is Jewish.
